description: Feeds back the outcome of a completed request so the limiter can honour Retry-After and widen its interval after repeated 429/5xx responses.
signature: def observe_response(self, status_code: int, headers: Mapping[str, str]) -> None
docstring:
Update limiter state from a response.

Args:
    status_code: The HTTP status code received.
    headers: Response headers, case-insensitively checked for 'Retry-After'.

Effects:
    On 429 with a parseable Retry-After header, the next acquire() call waits at least that many seconds, and the limiter's base interval is widened by a fixed multiplicative factor for the remainder of the run (invariant from the acquisition module spec's edge case: 'repeated 429 widens the base interval for the rest of the run'). On any 5xx, no interval widening occurs here (HttpClient's own backoff handles 5xx retries at the request level); observe_response only tracks 429s for interval widening. On 2xx/3xx/4xx-other, no state change beyond bookkeeping.
preconditions: status_code is a valid HTTP status integer
postconditions: After a 429 with Retry-After: N, the next acquire() call's wait is at least N seconds
After two consecutive 429s within the same run, the limiter's steady-state interval is strictly larger than its initial configured interval

A subsequent successful (2xx) response does not shrink the interval back down within the same run (widening is monotonic per run, matching the conservative 'defaults are deliberately pessimistic' design note)

edge_cases.input: status_code=429, headers without a Retry-After key
edge_cases.expected_behavior: falls back to the multiplicative backoff widening only, no explicit fixed-duration wait is injected
next acquire() waits at least 120 seconds

edge_cases.input: status_code=429, Retry-After='<HTTP-date>' (date form, e.g. 'Wed, 21 Oct 2026 07:28:00 GMT')
edge_cases.expected_behavior: parsed as an absolute time and converted to a relative wait; a date already in the past yields a wait of 0, not a negative number
no interval change; existing widening (if any) from earlier in the run persists

unit_tests.name: test_retry_after_seconds_form_widens_wait
unit_tests.description: Retry-After: 5 causes the next acquire() to wait at least 5 simulated seconds.

unit_tests.name: test_retry_after_http_date_form_parsed
unit_tests.description: An HTTP-date Retry-After in the near future is converted to a correct relative wait.
unit_tests.expected: next acquire() wait matches the date-derived delta within 1 second

unit_tests.name: test_repeated_429_widens_base_interval
unit_tests.description: Two consecutive 429 observations leave the limiter's steady-state interval larger than its construction-time value.

unit_tests.name: test_success_does_not_reset_widening
unit_tests.description: A 200 after two 429s does not shrink the interval back down.
